item.title: Young talent shines at Ngele'ia tag rugby tournament
item.description: Young rugby players have showcased their talent and potential at a tag rugby tournament hosted by the Ngele’ia Warlord Academy on Saturday, 29 August. The tournament brought together boys and girls from the academy’s junior age groups, to compete, develop their skills and enjoy rugby in a supportive environment.
item.content:encoded:
Young rugby players have showcased their talent and potential at a tag rugby tournament hosted by the Ngele’ia Warlord Academy on Saturday, 29 August.

The tournament brought together boys and girls from the academy’s junior age groups, to compete, develop their skills and enjoy rugby in a supportive environment.

The event also attracted children from outside Ngele’ia, with players joining from Lapaha and Nukunuku and other villages.

Academy founder and head coach Mike Dansey said he was encouraged by the growing interest among children and families.

The Ngele’ia Warlord Academy was established in the first week of August with only eight children. Within a month, more than 80 young people had joined from villages across Tongatapu.

“A parent showed up at the tournament on Saturday with their kid and said they just saw the poster on FaceBook and came all the way from Lapaha to have their kid participate, and some kids from Nukunuku too,” Dansey told Matangi Tonga.

The academy caters for boys and girls from Under-8 to Under-14 offering tag rugby, soccer and flag football\

“There are kids that may not be good at rugby but are good at other sports,” he said.

The academy runs tag rugby sessions on Mondays and Wednesdays, soccer on Tuesdays and Thursdays and flag football on Fridays, with activities held from 4.30pm to 5.30pm at the Ngele'ia Rugby Field beside the GPS Ngele'ia school.

“I wanted to start the academy to get kids out of the house and off their devices,” Dansey said.

The academy also aims to provide young people with positive activities and opportunities to develop discipline, teamwork and confidence hoping to ready young players for the Pacific games to be held here in 2031.

Dansey said his experience overseas had strengthened his desire to create a safe and positive sporting environment for children in Tonga.

The academy has received support from its ambassador, NRL player Konrad Hurrell, who has donated uniforms and sporting equipment. Rugby supporters and former players have also contributed to the programme.

Dansey encouraged communities to create more sporting spaces where young people could remain active, develop their abilities and pursue opportunities through sport.
